prerequisites: It is highly recommended that the student has acquired the competencies corresponding to the subjects of previous semesters.
The student must have a B1 Spanish certificate in the case of international mobility.

To acquire the competencies of the subjects at a sustained pace, it is recommended that the student is familiar with and has knowledge of the following subjects taken in previous semesters: Rigid Solid Mechanics. Kinematics and Dynamics of Machines and Mechanisms. Engineering materials, their properties and applications. Material forming processes. In-service behavior of materials. Loads, stresses and elastic and plastic deformations. Stress state. Plane and spatial geometry. Trigonometry. Differential and integral calculus. Vector algebra. Basic programming concepts. Computer science.

learning_outcomes.text: Understand the mechanical functioning of a robot.
Know the criteria that will guide them to evaluate the convenience of using a robot in a given industrial environment and the most appropriate way to do so.
Know the main types of robots and their characteristics.
Be able to identify the causes of mechanical failure or breakdown in robotic systems.

syllabus_topics: BLOCK A. INTRODUCTION TO ROBOTICS
A.1. Historical background of robotics.
A.2. Basic definitions in robotic technology.
A.3. Current applications of robotics. The future of robotics.
A.4. Basic market prospecting of current robotics.
A.5. Morphology of robots.
BLOCK B. ROBOTIC TECHNOLOGY
B.2. Electromechanical technology: Analysis, Design and Computational Simulation.
B.3. Fluid-mechanical technology: Analysis, Design and Computational Simulation.
BLOCK C. ROBOT SPATIAL LOCALIZATION
C.1. Position representation: Cartesian, cylindrical and spherical coordinates.
C.2. Orientation representation: rotation matrices.
C.3. Robot spatial localization: Homogeneous Transformation Matrices.
C.4. Euler angles and rotation pair.
C.5. Quaternion algebra.
C.6. Relationship between spatial localization methods.
C.7. Simulation of spatial localization in MATLAB.
BLOCK D. KINEMATIC ROBOTIC ANALYSIS
D.1. Introduction to robot kinematics.
D.2. Direct kinematic problem: geometric and analytical methods.
D.3. Denavit-Hartenberg algorithm.
D.4. Inverse kinematic problem: geometric and analytical methods.
D.5. Kinematic decoupling.
D.6. Differential model: analytical and geometric Jacobian.
D.7. Computational modeling in Matlab.
BLOCK E. DYNAMIC ROBOTIC ANALYSIS
E.1. The structural dynamic model of the robot. Euler's Law.
E.2. The dynamic model of the robot's actuators.
E.3. The dynamic model of the robot. Lagrange formulation.
teaching_methods: Expository, explanatory and/or demonstrative sessions of content (Theory)
Resolution of exercises and problems (Practice, seminars and problems)
Voluntary activities related to the subject developed in industrial and business contexts (Field trip practices)
Individual and autonomous study and work (Non-presential formative activities)
Personalized assistance in the formative process between the teacher and students, including resolving doubts (Tutoring activities)
Resolution of exercises and problems using computer tools or software (Computer practices)
Practical sessions in the Mechanical Engineering laboratory (Workshop/laboratory practices)

assessment_methods.method: Design and mechanical analysis of a robotized unit
Activities on the historical introduction, robotic technology and spatial localization tools
